claims.text: The baseline material is a thin FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate.
The controlled intervention is a moderate increase in Cu content relative to the baseline composition.
Increasing the relative Cu content enhances lattice distortion in FeNiCrCoCu.
Cu has a larger atomic-size difference relative to the other constituent elements.
The greater Cu concentration increases local lattice strain.
Enhanced lattice strain and associated pinning sites impede dislocation motion.
Enhanced lattice strain impedes dynamic recovery during high-temperature sliding.
Dynamic recovery contributes to microscopic plastic deformation during sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and dynamic recovery reduce cumulative microscopic deformation.
Reduced cumulative microscopic deformation leads to lower material removal and wear.
The Cu-enhanced coating will have lower wear volume than the baseline coating during high-temperature sliding.
The Cu-enhanced coating will exhibit less microscopic plastic deformation than the baseline coating during high-temperature sliding.
The prediction is intended to apply at approximately 600–700 °C under controlled load and sliding speed.
The prediction may not apply at lower temperatures or under radically different wear conditions.
Diffusion and recovery effects are thermally activated under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
Competing high-temperature softening mechanisms could counteract benefits attributed to increased lattice distortion.
